selection: Task3 grounding: seven existing answerable questions (q01, q13, q14, q16, q18, q19, q20) plus all three out-of-corpus controls (q21–q23). Fixed before generation; one RAG condition, ten answers.
review_basis: Expected facts recorded before generation from saved Task0 source snapshots. Full normalized source texts retained with line numbers; expected facts are never sent to the model.

questions.query: How can a function require an implicit service and how is that service resolved?

expected_facts.text: Declare context(name: Service) on the function for an implicit dependency.
Resolution happens at the call site by matching context values by type.
Multiple compatible values at the same scope level cause ambiguity.

questions.mistakes_to_watch: Do not present old context receivers as the current named-parameter syntax; distinguish experimental explicit arguments.
questions.selection_reason: Current context-parameter syntax, scope resolution and ambiguity.

questions.query: How are Kotlin exceptions exposed to Swift and Objective-C callers?

expected_facts.text: @Throws on non-suspend functions yields Swift throws and Objective-C NSError-producing methods.
Only listed exception classes and subclasses propagate as NSError; other escaping Kotlin exceptions terminate the program.
Suspend completion handlers always have an error parameter; without @Throws only CancellationException propagates, while non-suspend exceptions do not propagate.

questions.mistakes_to_watch: Do not claim arbitrary Kotlin exceptions are catchable from Swift.
questions.selection_reason: Exception propagation versus process termination across language boundaries.

questions.query: How does Swift export expose Kotlin suspend functions?

expected_facts.text: Swift export maps Kotlin suspend functions and suspending functional types to Swift async counterparts.
Swift calls the exported suspend function with try await, as shown in the saved guide.
Swift export is Alpha; distinguish its direct Swift mapping from the Objective-C completion-handler bridge.

questions.mistakes_to_watch: Do not claim Swift export lacks suspend support or conflate it with Objective-C framework export.
questions.selection_reason: Direct Swift export differs from the older Objective-C bridge.

questions.query: How do I declare an existing JavaScript API so Kotlin can call it without providing an implementation?

expected_facts.text: Use external on declarations whose implementation is supplied by JavaScript.
Do not provide a Kotlin body; the compiler emits no implementation and JavaScript must supply it.
external is package-level and inherited by nested members; optional JS arguments can use definedExternally.

questions.mistakes_to_watch: Do not present Kotlin/Wasm-only JsAny restrictions as universal Kotlin/JS requirements; distinguish imports from exports.
questions.selection_reason: Both Task0 chunkers missed the designated Kotlin/JS source section, retrieving Wasm neighbors.

questions.query: When did the common Kotlin UUID API become stable?

relevant.section: Stable UUID API in the common Kotlin standard library

expected_facts.text: The common kotlin.uuid.Uuid API became Stable in Kotlin 2.4.0.
V4 and V7 generation functions remain Experimental and require opt-in.
The API was introduced experimentally in Kotlin 2.0.20; introduction and stabilization differ.

questions.mistakes_to_watch: Do not confuse 2.0.20 introduction with stability or claim all UUID APIs are stable.
questions.selection_reason: Exact stabilization release with experimental exceptions.

questions.query: What changed in Kotlin 2.4.20 for exporting suspending lambdas to JavaScript?

relevant.section: Support for exporting suspending lambdas as async functions

expected_facts.text: Kotlin 2.4.20 supports exporting suspending lambdas as JavaScript async functions.
Enable -Xsuspend-lambda-exporting.
Annotate relevant declarations @JsExport; compiler bridges suspend lambdas with JS async/await.

questions.mistakes_to_watch: Do not substitute older Promise wrappers or say no such support exists.
questions.selection_reason: A version-specific compiler flag and async bridge introduced in 2.4.20.

questions.query: Which Kotlin 2.4.20 feature permits Swift implementations to extend exported Kotlin types?

expected_facts.text: Kotlin 2.4.20 introduces cross-language inheritance in Swift export.
The reverse-import pattern declares a Kotlin interface and open Kotlin base class; Swift subclasses the base and implements the interface.
Pass the Swift instance to Kotlin functions accepting the interface so Kotlin dispatches to Swift code.

questions.mistakes_to_watch: Do not claim inheritance is forbidden or omit the Kotlin superclass required by the documented pattern.
questions.selection_reason: New cross-language inheritance and reverse-import requirements in 2.4.20.
